boundaries.conclusion: The observer entry point requires root, aarch64, and exactly one explicit rock.ui.auth.verify=1 boot token.

The only runtime boundary_probe call follows a fresh USD simulator/empty-row check and environment validation. environment() checks the dedicated authenticator process, seccomp, directory ownership/type and production modes.
The verification harness injects this observer and its flag-guarded startup hook into a new rootfs copy only. The ordinary platform installer does not install guest-ui-auth-evidence.py.
The harness creates a separate test rootfs and new userdata, boots QEMU with no network and a read-only copied rootfs, and checks original images/source hashes afterward.

Directory 0755 and socket 0666 deliberately remove DAC barriers for a negative peer-UID check. The directory remains unwritable to other UIDs. The observer sends only auth.status and snapshot reads; no credentials or mutation requests are issued.

The actual authenticator rejects every nonowner peer UID from SO_PEERCRED before reading the request body. The daemon retains four bounded slots and finite deadlines; widening socket DAC does not bypass this authorization.
Authenticator data directory 0700 and database 0600 are checked and not relaxed by boundary_probe; the socket permission changes do not grant database/file access.
Ordinary completion and exceptions enter finally and restore socket 0660 then directory 0750. The restored:true result is returned only if both restoration calls succeed.

The host harness detects observer failure and its finally closes the monitor and terminates then kills its own QEMU child if still running. This bounds persistence of test-guest runtime permission changes; it does not modify the source image or another live device.

followUpCycles.status: empty HTTPS CA rejected before network; same-SHA publication checks pending

focusedFinding.description: The HTTPS constructor rejected only ca_file is None, while context creation and TLS wrapping used truthiness. Empty string, False and zero passed the guard but produced no SSLContext; assigning the raw socket to HTTPSConnection bypassed its implicit connect/handshake. The client accepted a normal plaintext discovery response while describing its transport as HTTPS.
focusedFinding.reachability: Confirmed through the public MCPHttpClient constructor with locally supplied malformed CA configuration. The reviewed production runtime caller currently selects its intentional loopback HTTP fixture; no external request or deployed configuration path to choose an empty HTTPS CA was established.
focusedFinding.impact: For this API/configuration path, the HTTPS promise was not enforced and a public synthetic Authorization header reached a plaintext loopback listener. This does not establish exposure of an actual credential, selected user data or deployed service.

followUpCycles.originalAlertAssessment: The two flagged calls wrap owned loopback synthetic test servers with PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER and an existing public fixture certificate/key. This host has TLS1.2 minimum by default. No change was made to those fixture contexts and no alert dismissal or resolution is claimed.

change.description: Reject any falsey CA for HTTPS before socket activity. Preserve the existing SSLContext creation and all HTTP fixture behavior. Successful HTTPS construction now necessarily follows the existing truthy-CA branch and creates a validating context.
change.whyNoAdditionalContextBranchChange: Changing context creation to scheme-based would also change the existing HTTP-plus-CA combination outside the proven gap. The guard matches the existing truthy predicate and closes the verified path without that unrelated behavior change.

before.meaning: The new test runs against the original production source; None was already rejected, while the five other falsey inputs incorrectly constructed a client.

after.meaning: The existing 30 tests plus the new one pass. Owned real loopback HTTPS with the public CA, explicit HTTP fixture, wire deadlines, no automatic effect retry, envelope bindings and private configuration checks remain covered.

sourceFacts.fact: Origin credentials/path/query/fragment are refused; literal IP required. HTTP requires allow_http_fixture is True and exact 127.0.0.1; HTTPS requires an explicit nonempty CA.

HTTPS contexts use create_default_context with the configured CA and wrap_socket(server_hostname=literal host). The descriptor includes the configured CA file digest; this is not asserted to be an SPKI or exact leaf-certificate pin.
HubClient is a separate development client limited to HTTPS 127.0.0.1/10.0.2.2 with explicit port and no URL credentials, query or fragment.
The Hub CA is loaded through NOFOLLOW/NONBLOCK, checked as bounded regular owner/root-owned non-writable file. A byte digest participates in retained configuration binding.
HubClient uses PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT and explicit TLS1.2 minimum, loads CA bytes and validates the configured server host.
Existing protected binding includes profile, gateway configuration and CA SHA256, and configuration drift remains unavailable instead of rebinding silently.
The development gateway requires a loopback bind and explicitly sets TLS1.2 minimum for its server context.
The current runtime uses the explicit local HTTP provider fixture, then serves its device-facing gateway over TLS. No call-site configuration expansion was introduced.
